Compare hierarchical administrative names between two datasets

Source: R/compare_adm_div.R
compare_adm_div.Rd

This function compares sets of administrative unit names between two datasets at a given hierarchical level. For each parent administrative unit at the previous level, it identifies names that are present in one dataset but not the other.

Usage

compare_adm_div(x, y, level = 1)

Arguments

x

A data frame or tibble containing administrative unit names. Must include a column named adm_div_<level> and, if level > 1, columns adm_div_1, ..., adm_div_(level - 1).

y

A data frame or tibble with the same structure as x.

level

Integer scalar. Administrative level to compare. Must correspond to a column adm_div_<level>. If greater than 1, grouping is performed by the full chain of ancestor columns adm_div_1, ..., adm_div_(level - 1), not just the immediate parent.

Value

A tibble with one row per parent administrative unit combination containing:

level

The level of comparison

parent

The parent administrative unit chain, concatenated with " || " when level > 1 (or "ALL" for level 1)

x_only

Character vector of names present only in x

y_only

Character vector of names present only in y

Details

The comparison is hierarchical:

  • level = 1: global comparison (all observations grouped together)

  • level > 1: comparison is performed within each unique combination of adm_div_1, ..., adm_div_(level - 1)

For each parent group, the function returns:

  • names present only in x

  • names present only in y

The parent key is constructed by concatenating all ancestor administrative levels using " || " as a separator. This means two units at the same level sharing a name (e.g. two districts both called "Central") will only be treated as a match if their entire ancestor chain is identical — a "Central" district under Region A / Province X is never pooled with a "Central" district under Region A / Province Y, or under an entirely different region.

Internally, the function:

  • concatenates ancestor columns into a single parent key

  • selects unique combinations of parent key and name

  • removes missing values in the name column

  • aggregates names per parent into sorted lists

  • performs a full join between datasets at the parent level

  • computes set differences using setdiff()

The helper function build_name_sets() is used internally to construct grouped name lists but is not exported.

Examples

x <- data.frame(adm_div_1 = c("North", "North", "South"),
                adm_div_2 = c("Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma"))
y <- data.frame(adm_div_1 = c("North", "North", "South"),
                adm_div_2 = c("Alpha", "Betta", "Gamma"))

compare_adm_div(x, y, level = 1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   level parent x_only    y_only   
#>   <dbl> <chr>  <list>    <list>   
#> 1     1 ALL    <chr [0]> <chr [0]>
compare_adm_div(x, y, level = 2)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   level parent x_only    y_only   
#>   <dbl> <chr>  <list>    <list>   
#> 1     2 North  <chr [1]> <chr [1]>
#> 2     2 South  <chr [0]> <chr [0]>
